title: [Question] How to specify sortOrder from custom widget
body:
**Component**

 * UI

**Description**
I try to specify a sortOrder into a pageLink to get my results sorted (in this case devices sorted by name).

**Environment**
 * OS:  name and version
 * ThingsBoard: 3.1 PE
 * Browser: Firefox

When developing custom widget you can request devices assigned to a certain customer using this call:
`self.ctx.deviceService.getCustomerDevices(customerId, pageLink).subscribe(....`

This works fine with default pageLink that you obtain like this:

`self.ctx.pageLink()`; 

or even like this 

`self.ctx.pageLink(200, 0, '', null);  `

where 200 is the max page size, 0 is the current page, '' is the search string and I guess last parameter is the sortOrder.

Now I don't know how to specify sortOrder. The closest I got was with this:
```
       var pl = self.ctx.pageLink(200, 0, '', null);
       pl['sortOrder'] = {};
       pl.sortOrder['direction'] = 'ASC';
       pl.sortOrder['key'] = {};
       pl.sortOrder.key['key'] = 'name';
       pl.sortOrder.key['type'] = 'ENTITY_FIELD';
```

which succeed to inject sortOrder in the request but not the sortProperty.

/devices?pageSize=200&page=0&sortProperty=undefined&sortOrder=ASC&type=

Logically resulting in a 500 server error with that error:

`org.hibernate.QueryException: could not resolve property: undefined of: org.thingsboard.server.dao.model.sql.DeviceEntity [SELECT d FROM org.thingsboard.server.dao.model.sql.DeviceEntity d WHERE d.tenantId = :tenantId AND d.customerId = :customerId AND LOWER(d.searchText) LIKE LOWER(CONCAT(:searchText, '%')) order by d.undefined asc]; nested exception is java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: org.hibernate.QueryException: could not resolve property: undefined of: org.thingsboard.server.dao.model.sql.DeviceEntity [SELECT d FROM org.thingsboard.server.dao.model.sql.DeviceEntity d WHERE d.tenantId = :tenantId AND d.customerId = :customerId AND LOWER(d.searchText) LIKE LOWER(CONCAT(:searchText, '%')) order by d.undefined asc]`

So what is the proper way of performing this request with sort order on a field?
author: bbrenne

comments.body: Try `self.ctx.pageLink(200, 0, '', {property: 'YOUR_KEY_NAME', direction: 'ASC'});`
It's working, thanks a lot.

satisfaction_conditions: A correct syntax for specifying sort order in a pageLink object
A solution that allows sorting devices by a specific field
A working approach that doesn't result in server errors
A simple, concise implementation method

title: [Question] How can thingsboard gateway connect multiple OPC servers?
body:
The usage scenario is as follows: each device has an independent OPC server. Now I can correctly collect the device through the thingsboard gateway, but opcua In the configuration of JSON, the address of an OPC server corresponding to each device cannot be configured.
In the seemingly TB configuration, the "opc-ua" scenario only supports one server corresponding to multiple devices.
How can I configure the gateway to support one configuration and access all devices?

I need to configure an array "server"？
or
I need to configure multiple "opcua. json"
author: bggmjxh

comments.body:
You need to move this question to thingsboad-gateway project.
But I try to answer. You can create multiple configuration files opcua1. json, opcua2. json, opcua3. json and link each of them to corresponding OPC UA connector in the gateway configuration file. For example:
```yaml
connectors:
  -
    name: 1 OPC
    type: opcua
    configuration: opcua1.json
  -
    name: 2 OPC
    type: opcua
    configuration: opcua2.json
```
@devaskim Thanks very much!

title: [Question] how to setup a staging environment in clustered mode - licence key conflict
body:
**Component**
 * Installation

**Description**
I'm trying to setup a staging environment in my company to test changes for my tenants before applying them on the production environment.
Both environments are running TB PE 3.3.1 with hybrid storage (postgres+cassandra).
I want the staging environment to be a copy of the production environment data-wise, so I purchased another TB licence to run the staging environment, then tried to dump & restore the postgres database from the production instance on the staging instance.
However the production database somehow contains the licence information embedded in it.
Now my staging environment does not start and I have no idea how to reapply my 2nd license key while keeping the rest of the data.

How should I proceed ?

**Environment**
 * OS:  ubuntu
 * ThingsBoard: 3.3.1PE running on docker-compose
author: ThomasPrioul

comments.body:
There is no license information in the database. All the license info is stored in the license.data file. Maybe you have copied the volumes (and not only the database). Then this is the root cause. Just
1) shut down dev TB instance
2) remove the license.data file
3) make sure the correct license key is used.
4) start it again.

Thanks for your answer.
I had probably corrupted something else, my TB instance was not starting and I had no license.data file at all.
What I did was **remove the old instance from the license server**, reset everything and the staging instance came back to life.
I had not copied the volume, I did a SQL dump from the running postgres container in production.

satisfaction_conditions: A solution for resolving license key conflicts when setting up a staging environment
Information about where ThingsBoard PE stores license information
A procedure to reset or reapply a license in ThingsBoard PE

Hello @KenSense,

Also, we strongly recommend backing up your database before any upgrade.

The question was in case I'm stuck is there a way to go back to the previous version assuming you have a backup of the database before you started the upgrade or is full VM restore advised/required?

If you have a database backup, of course, you can revert to a previous version. For example, you had a version 3.3.1, and you failed to upgrade to 3.3.2:

Just run the old install and script again?

In your case: when you only restore the backup, you need just run your thingsboard service and didn't install any (Or delete files).


I advise you to try these actions on some virtual machine so that there is no misunderstanding of backup algorithms on your main server.

title: Device Profile Alarm Rule - alarm severity cannot be change from Critical to Major
body:
Consider the following device profile alarm rule:
creation condition 1: if device temperature > 4, create High Temperature alarm with Critical severity
creation condition 2: if device temperature > 0 and temperature <=4, create High Temperature alarm with Major severity
clear condition: if device temperature < 0

Test result:
1. device temperature = 2, new alarm with Major severity is created => OK
2. device temperature = 5, alarm is updated with Critical Severity => OK
3. device temperature = 2 again, no update to alarm severity => NOT OK
4. device temperature = -1, alarm is cleared => OK

Question: in step 3,  should the alarm be updated with severity set to Major?
author: sunyong-mwi

comments.body: It is currently implemented the way you described. For us, it seems logical and expected behavior. We assume the person who is configuring the rule is interested to know about the alarm caused by the "maximum" temperature. For example, if this is a fridge with something that can't be stored with temperature > 0. Then, if the temperature is -2 it is Major alarm, but if the temperature was +1, it is definitely critical, even if then, the temperature is back to -2.
Thanks for the explanation. I understood the logic behind now.

satisfaction_conditions: An explanation of the logical reasoning behind the current alarm severity behavior
Clarification about the intended design of the alarm system's severity handling
A practical use case that demonstrates why the current behavior is beneficial

title: Is there a way to hide a widget based on device type?
body:
**Component**
Dashboard states

 * UI
Multiple dashboard for devices

**Description**
Is there a way to hide a widget based on the device type that's clicked?  For Example I have an entity list widget with all my devices on my first landing page dashboard.  The user clicks on the device and it goes to a dashboard state with detailed info.  I have devices that are very similar but may or may not have an extra feature such as humidity.  So basically if I have a device with temperature and humidity I want to show the graphs of temperature and humidity when I click on that type of device.  If I have a device with only temperature the info dashboard should have no humidity graph.  

Is the only way to do this with multiple dashboards?  The issue I have with that is there are several other widgets on the info page and if I make a change to one of those other widgets I now have to duplicate the change on the other dashboards....

**Environment**
 * OS:  Windows Server 2016
 * ThingsBoard: 2.3.4
 * Browser: Chrome (latest version)
author: sferguson-ISI

comments.body:
Hello,
There is no option to hide a widget from a particular state but in your case, you could create a second state (not a new dashboard), and when clicking on a device in the list check its type and depending on this navigate to the needed state. As for widgets that should be the same for both states (only if they are completely the same including a datasource set, state entity for example), there is an ability to copy widget by link. If the widget copied by link, changes made to it in one state should be automatically propagated to another.

Depending on your widgets, you could also apply a filter which will check for attribute or timeseries "humidity". E.g. applying an attribute filter "Humidity" with key name "humidity" you can set operation to "ignore case" if this attribute "not contains" a value (you leave the value line blank). Now if you have a widget where you want to display your humidity and temperature timeseries, simply create an extra datasource which will apply the filter for each device depending on your dashboard state.

> Hello,
> There is no option to hide a widget from a particular state but in your case, you could create a second state (not a new dashboard), and when clicking on a device in the list check its type and depending on this navigate to the needed state. As for widgets that should be the same for both states (only if they are completely the same including a datasource set, state entity for example), there is an ability to copy widget by link. If the widget copied by link, changes made to it in one state should be automatically propagated to another.

This was a good workaround and prevents me from having to duplicate widget code changes.  For anyone else looking at this, when you click on a widget there is an option to "Copy" or "Copy Reference" do the later. thanks!
